## Summary

Redesigned "Host on Bilko.run" from a 1-project-per-app model to a **1-project = 1-Bilko-listing = N-documents** model, matching your requirement:

- **Data model** (`session-manager-operations/bilko-host/documents.json`): one root document (`subpath: ''` → `dist/index.html` → `bilko.run/projects/<app-name>/`, defaults to the Marketing Project Page) plus any number of sub-path documents (`subpath: 'special-doc/01'` → `dist/special-doc/01/index.html` → `bilko.run/projects/<app-name>/special-doc/01/`). Sources can be another generated Project Page lens or an arbitrary local HTML file.
- **Deletion, confirmed not guessed**: I read Bilko's actual `publish_static_project` implementation (`mcp-host-server/src/server.ts`) — it does `rm -rf` then `cp -r` the *entire* `public/projects/<slug>/` tree on every publish, never a merge. So Stage A (`prepareBundle`) always wipes and rebuilds `dist/` from the current document list, and the next Publish is guaranteed to remove anything you deleted locally — no separate delete API needed on Bilko's side, and no risk of orphaned live pages after a "successful" delete.
- **Left-nav tab** (`HostBilko.tsx`): document list with live-URL previews, Add (sub-path + title + source lens) and Remove per row, a staleness indicator (`bundleStale`) so removing a document visibly shows "not yet live-removed until you Publish" rather than implying it's already gone.
- Rewired `src/main/bilkoHost.cjs` (+ new pure `bilkoHostCore.cjs`) and IPC/preload types for the multi-document model.
- **Caught and fixed a real bug while testing**: `config.cjs`'s `validateWrite` has a second, separate allowlist gate on top of the `OWNERS` law — every existing namespace (`browser`, `feedback`, `prompt-sessions`, `scheduler`, `project-brief`) needs its own carve-out there too, and I'd missed it for `bilko-host`. Without it, every write in `bilkoHost.cjs` would have thrown at runtime despite passing typecheck. Added the carve-out; documented the two-gate quirk in the architecture doc so it doesn't get missed again.
- Updated the architecture doc and the `bilko-host-publisher` agent persona to describe the multi-document/whole-tree-replace model.
- New tests: `bilkoHostCore.test.cjs` (subpath/document-set validation, path/URL math) and `bilkoHost-integration.test.cjs` (real temp-dir add/remove/rebuild, explicitly asserting a removed document's file is gone after rebuild).

# Bilko.run Integration — What Was Built

## The idea

Session Manager builds projects; Bilko.run is Stanislav's own hosting platform. This integration adds a **"Host on Bilko.run"** left-nav tab (Configure group, per-project) that publishes a project's already-generated marketing content to bilko.run with a few clicks — using Bilko's *existing* self-service publish infrastructure rather than inventing a new one.

## Key discovery that shaped the design

Bilko.run already ships `mcp-host-server` — an MCP server built specifically so sibling repos can publish themselves *without* hand-editing the Bilko repo: `register_static_project`, `publish_static_project` (gated by 5 checks — manifest schema, size budget, a Playwright "golden path" smoke test, an a11y scan, `pnpm audit`), and `status`. I read its actual source rather than guessing, which surfaced the one fact the whole delete story depends on: **every publish does `rm -rf` then `cp -r` the entire target directory** — a full replace, never a merge. That single confirmed behavior is what makes local deletion reliably propagate live, with no separate "delete" API needed.

## The data model: one Bilko project, many hosted documents

A Bilko "static-path" app is just one directory tree served at `bilko.run/projects/<slug>/`. Nothing stops that tree from containing more than one page — so instead of 1 project ↔ 1 URL, the model is 1 project ↔ **N documents**:

- **Root document** (`subpath: ''`) → `dist/index.html` → `bilko.run/projects/<slug>/` — "the project itself," defaults to the Marketing Project Page.
- **Sub-path documents** (`subpath: 'special-doc/01'`) → `dist/special-doc/01/index.html` → `bilko.run/projects/<slug>/special-doc/01/` — any number of additional explanatory pages, each independently added/removed.

This directly answers "I don't want 3 Bilko projects for 1 project with extra docs" and "I should be able to post all 4 of Project Pages' generated HTMLs" — for Session Manager itself, that's Marketing (root) + Home/Feature/Architecture (sub-paths), one Bilko listing, 4 unique URLs.

## Two-stage pipeline

- **Stage A — Bundle prep** (`src/main/bilkoHost.cjs`, deterministic, no LLM): rebuilds the whole `dist/` tree from `documents.json` on every run (`rm` then rewrite) — this wholesale-replace is what guarantees a removed document can never linger on disk, mirroring Bilko's own publish semantics.
- **Stage B — Publish** (an Epic tagged `bilko-host-publisher`, new local agent persona): drives the actual `bilko-host` MCP calls. Deliberately agent-driven rather than hardcoded in the main process, because Bilko's gate implementations can change independently — the agent is instructed to read the gate source live each run instead of trusting a cached understanding. It never bypasses a failing gate on its own initiative; that's always a human call.

## UI (`HostBilko.tsx`)

- Compatibility gate (needs a generated Marketing page first; confirms before publishing a `private` package).
- Slug field, **Prepare Bundle**, **Publish** buttons; bundle/publish status with a "bundle out of date" warning when the document list has changed since the last build.
- **Hosted documents** list — add a document (sub-path + title + source), remove one (takes effect on next Publish, never pretends to be live before it is).
- **Project Pages quick-add panel** — one row per lens (Home/Marketing/Feature/Architecture) showing root/hosted/available, a **"+ Host as /‹lens›/"** button per lens, and **"Host all N remaining"** for one-click bulk publish of everything Project Pages generated.

## Wiring underneath

New `EpicTag` (`bilko-host-publisher`) + agent persona, new `bilko-host` OWNERS namespace (plus a `config.cjs` write-boundary carve-out I discovered was also required — caught by an integration test, not just unit tests), new IPC endpoints (`get`/`prepare-bundle`/`add-document`/`remove-document`), `.mcp.json` wired to Bilko's publish server, and a full architecture spec at `session-manager-operations/architecture/bilko-host-integration.md` documenting all of the above as the source of truth for future changes.

## Verification

Typecheck, selector-lint, and every Bilko-host-related test suite (unit tests for the pure logic, an integration test against a real temp project dir proving a removed document actually disappears from `dist/` after rebuild) all pass. Not implemented: the actual live publish execution (that's the Epic's job at runtime by design) and a file-picker UI for custom (non-Project-Page) HTML sources — the backend supports it, the UI only exposes the Project Page lenses today.
